text:
Edmonton's record says contender and its chances say coin flip, and the gap between those two things is the whole story of the Oilers' season. They are 17-7-4, but they get only 49.5% of the expected goals (47% at five on five) and have scored about 25 more goals than their chances deserve, the biggest finishing surplus in our tables.

Much of that is simply Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl. With Vasily Podkolzin on their wing they have 59% of the expected goals and a 23-10 goal edge in 286 minutes, and Evan Bouchard with Mattias Ekholm is plus 16 in goals. Elite shooters do beat expected goals, so not all of the surplus is luck. The worry is everyone else: the Mathieu Joseph, Alex Formenton and Owen Michaels line gets 31% of the expected goals, and the Connor Murphy and Ryan Shea pair, which plays the most minutes of any Edmonton pair, gets 43%.

That depth problem showed in a five-game winless run this month, in which the Oilers got 45% of the expected goals. Ryan Nugent-Hopkins is back from a five-game absence, while Zach Hyman remained out, per Sportsnet. In net, Devon Levi had a rough night against Carolina.

Our numbers still give Edmonton a 95% chance at the playoffs, because the points are banked. What we'd watch: whether Mike Babcock's team can win the minutes when McDavid sits, because that is where this record will be tested.
